Engagement at capture: 183 likes, 441 bookmarks (~2.4:1 bookmark:like — genuine save-for-later signal), ~44.6k views (fxtwitter).

## Summary

Two macOS window managers, one per tweet in the chain:

- **Ribbon** ([meetribbon.app](https://meetribbon.app)) — via @abhijitwt. "A scrolling window manager for Mac": windows stay full height on one continuous strip, new windows open beside the current one instead of shrinking or stacking, and **SIP stays on** (no system-integrity disable). **Pay once** (no subscription).
- **Shoji** ([shojimac.com](https://shojimac.com)) — via @Ankur_Sehrawatt. Automatic window tiling: "tiles every window the moment it opens. No dragging, no resizing, no layouts to set up." Has a live try-in-browser demo on the site.

Both verified live at capture (titles + og descriptions fetched). Pricing detail beyond Ribbon's "pay once" not captured.

## Why it matters

Window-manager recs are the highest-save-rate tweet genre for a reason: it's a daily-friction fix. The interesting contrast is the philosophy split — Ribbon keeps everything maximized on a horizontal scroll strip (spatial, zellij/tabs-as-windows), Shoji auto-tiles on open (hands-off, tiling-WM classic). The meme format ("thank me later" ×2) is engagement bait, but the bookmark ratio says people are actually saving these.

**Skepticism gates:** neither app is verified beyond its landing page (no reviews, no longevity check — the macOS window-manager graveyard is large; apps that hook window events die on macOS releases). If a Mac enters the picture, trial both briefly rather than paying immediately; check Shoji's model (site doesn't lead with pricing).

No action — reference pick for whenever macOS window management comes up.
